purpose: Desmopressin is used to treat bedwetting in children, frequent nighttime urination in adults, diabetes insipidus (a condition where your body makes too much urine), and certain bleeding disorders like mild hemophilia A and von Willebrand disease. It helps your body hold onto water so you do not urinate as much. It can also help your blood clot better in some bleeding conditions.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes a hormone called ADH (antidiuretic hormone) that tells your kidneys to hold onto water. Desmopressin is a man-made version of that hormone that works the same way. It signals your kidneys to absorb more water back into your body instead of sending it out as urine, which reduces how much you urinate. In bleeding disorders, it also helps release clotting factors stored in your blood vessel walls to help stop bleeding.
common_side_effects: Headache, nausea, stomach pain, stuffy or runny nose (with nasal forms), flushing or redness of the skin, and mild swelling. Some people feel dizzy or have a slight drop in blood pressure.
warnings: The most serious risk is low sodium levels in your blood (called hyponatremia), which can cause seizures, confusion, or even be life-threatening — this is especially risky in children and elderly patients. Do not drink too much water or fluids while taking this medication. Tell your doctor right away if you feel confused, have a headache, feel nauseated, or have swelling. Avoid this medication if you have kidney problems, heart failure, or are prone to fluid retention. Always take the lowest effective dose.
typical_dosing: Doses vary a lot depending on what it is being used for and your age. For bedwetting in children, a common dose is one tablet (0.2 mg) taken by mouth at bedtime. For nighttime urination in adults, a low-dose tablet (like 27.7 mcg or 50 mcg) is placed under the tongue at bedtime. For diabetes insipidus, doses range from 0.1 to 0.4 mg by mouth daily in divided doses. Your doctor will find the right dose for you — always follow their specific instructions.
